title: La serenata
desc: Midnight on the twenty-ninth of May, three musicians, and a woman pretending to be surprised
setting: It is five to twelve at night, you are standing in the street outside doña Elena's door, and Julio has paid the musicians.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: A las doce en punto empiezan. Vos cantás con nosotros, cuñado.
steps.en: They start at twelve on the dot. You sing with us, brother-in-law.

options.es: Yo canto muy mal, pero canto.
options.en: I sing terribly, but I will sing.
options.feedback: So do her three sons, every year. Singing badly in the street at midnight is the entire point of a serenata.

options.es: Yo no me sé la canción.
options.en: I do not know the song.
options.feedback: Nor does half the street. Stand with them and move your mouth.
You are her daughter's husband standing in the street at midnight. There is no version of tonight where you watch.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¡Ay, Dios mío! ¿Y esto qué es? ¡A esta hora!
steps.en: Oh my goodness! And what is this? At this hour!

options.feedback: She knew. She has known since March, she is standing at the door in her dressing gown, and everybody pretends every year. Play it straight.
Obviously. Explaining it takes the air out of the surprise she is performing.
Of course she knew. Saying so is the one thing that can spoil the twelve minutes she waits all year for.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Pasen, pasen. Voy a hacer café.
steps.en: Come in, come in. I will make coffee.

options.es: Con permiso, doña. Yo le ayudo con las tazas.
options.en: Excuse me, doña. I will help you with the cups.
options.feedback: Half past midnight and she is making coffee for eight people. Getting up to help is worth more to her than the song was.
Fine. Everyone else has already sat down and she is on her feet.

options.es: No se moleste, doña, ya nos vamos.
options.en: Do not trouble yourself, doña, we are going now.
options.feedback: Nobody is going anywhere. The coffee at one in the morning is the second half of the serenata.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Y usted, mijo. Gracias por venir con ellos.
steps.en: And you, son. Thank you for coming with them.

options.es: Es lo menos que puedo hacer, doña. Y con mucho cariño.
options.en: It is the least I can do, doña. And gladly.
options.feedback: That is the right register and it is not a cold one here. She has just called you mijo, which is the thing that actually happened tonight.
Polite. She said something to you that she does not say lightly and you answered a formula.
True and disastrous. You have just told her you came because you were told to.
